born in Liverpool, England, January 20, 1734; immigrated to the United States in 1747 and settled in Oxford, Md.; attended school in Philadelphia; became a merchant in Philadelphia in 1748; signed the non-importation agreement of 1765; member of the Pennsylvania Council of Safety, 1775; Delegate to the Second Continental Congress, 1775-1778; signed the Declaration of Independence; settled upon the Manheim estate; member, Pennsylvania state assembly, 1778-1781; national superintendent of finance, 1781-1784; established the Bank of North America; member, Pennsylvania state assembly, 1785-1787; delegate to the Federal Constitutional Convention in 1787; signed the U.S. Constitution; elected to the United States Senate and served from March 4, 1789, to March 3, 1795; declined to be a candidate for renomination; declined the position of Secretary of the Treasury in the Cabinet of President George Washington; known as the "financier of the American Revolution" and one of the richest men in America, Morris became involved in unsuccessful land speculations, which caused him to be imprisoned for debt from 1798 to 1801; died in Philadelphia, Pa., May 8, 1806; interment in the family vault of William White in the churchyard of Christ Church.CongressesCongressPositionPartyStateThe 2nd Continental CongressDelegatePennsylvania1SenatorPro-AdministrationPennsylvania2SenatorPro-AdministrationPennsylvania3SenatorPro-AdministrationPennsylvaniaThe 2nd Continental CongressThe 1st United States CongressThe 2nd United States CongressThe 3rd United States CongressBibliographyExtended BibliographyChernow, Barbara Ann.
